rows: Trees blown down across the county.
A tree fell on a power line.
The Hearne Fire Department reported a tornado on the ground near the Milam/Robertson County line. No damage was reported.
A brief touchdown was reported on the southeast edge of Bremond. The tornado downed power lines and damaged trees.
A tornado was observed by the Bremond Fire Department and the public near Petteway. Numerous trees were downed or damaged along its path.
The Franklin Fire Department reported a brief touchdown. No damage was reported.
A tree was blown down and partially blocked FM 46.
Golfball-size hail reported west of Marquez.
The Hearne AWOS measured a 64 mph wind gust.

Large cedar trees were uprooted and large limbs broken on the south side of Franklin. Additional tree damage was reported elsewhere in town along with downed power lines and broken windows. A motorcycle was also thrown across the road.
A brief tornado near Easterly tore down trees, fences, and power lines.
A brief tornado touchdown occurred near OSR and Edge Cutoff Road. A dust swirl was noted by the public but no damage was reported.
Quarter size hail was reported 1 mile west of Franklin.
Numerous trees were blown down in the city of Calvert.
Several large trees were blown down by thunderstorm gusts in the city of Hearne. Power was also out for most of the city.
Penny size hail covered the ground in Bremond.
Half-dollar size hail fell along Farm-to-Market Road 46 about 5 miles southeast of Bremond.
Hail up to the size of golfballs fell about 8 miles north of Franklin.
Quarter size hail was reported between Calvert and Hearne.
Quarter size hail covered the ground in Hearne.
Multiple trees were blown over about 6 miles west of Hearne. Trees were blown over across several county roads and Farm-to-Market 2095.
Nickel sized hail was reported in Hearne.
Penny sized hail was reported north of Calvert.
Hail increased to the size of a half dollar in Franklin.
Nickel sized hail was reported 2 miles southeast of Hearne.
Strong thunderstorm winds knocked down large trees and power poles near Jack Corn Rd and East Highway 79 near Easterly.
Law enforcement reported 8 trees down between Franklin and Bremond, TX, with some of them blocking roads.
A trained spotter reported half dollar sized hail in the city of Franklin.
Robertson County Sheriff's Department reported that the roof was blown off of a house in Calvert, TX, and that trees were reported down across the county.
A picture of an overturned trailer at LSP Trucking Facility was received from a member of the general public.
Franklin Volunteer Fire Department reported damage to outbuildings and damage to shingles; and that numerous trees were either snapped or uprooted and utility poles were blown down.
A 60 MPH wind gust was reported at the Lake Limestone RAWS site.
Robertson County Sheriff's Department reported trees down along Highway 7; approximately 12 miles north of Easterly.
Broadcast media reported that a roof was blown off of a laundromat and onto Hwy 79 in Frankin, TX.
A social media report indicated quarter size hail in Calvert.
Calvert Police Department reported several trees blocking a couple of roads near the city of Calvert, TX.
Robertson County Sheriff's Department reported roof damage in the city of Calvert, TX.
Fire and Rescue reported several trees down in the community of Elliot, just to the north-northeast of the city of Hearne, TX.
The Hearne, TX AWOS reported a peak wind gust of 59 MPH.
A public report indicated quarter-sized hail near the intersection of FM 2549 and FM 391, approximately 4 miles east-northeast of the city of Hearne, TX.
Broadcast media reported hail slightly larger than quarters in the city of Calvert, TX.
Broadcast media reported wind damage to a metal farm shed and a mobile home along and south of Highway 391 near the city of Hearne, TX.
A brief rope tornado occurred approximately 5 miles northwest of the city of Calvert, TX. The tornado was rated EF-0, lasted less than 30 seconds and produced no known damage.
A social media report indicated quarter size hail in the city of Bremond, TX.
A trained spotter reported nickel size hail in the city of Hearne, TX.
